reasons: The rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding Customer, so a document with no such covenant is correctly classified as compliant rather than missing — absence here benefits our party and should not be flagged.

Evidence of absence is well supported: no 'solicit', 'induce' or 'recruit' hits; the residual 'employ'/'personnel'/'hire' matches are in indemnity, damages-exclusion, confidentiality and data-security contexts; the miscellaneous provisions run (a)–(i) with no gap; and the survival list at p0070 omits any restrictive covenant.
The independent-contractor clause at p0066 disclaims an employment relationship only and imposes no hiring or solicitation restriction, so it does not create an implied covenant.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs.

The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are inapplicable because they measure the wording of an existing non-solicit; their failure is not evidence of error here.
